seg_share|USA|Product Format|Value: Gummies are expected to gain 496 BPS of value share as they overcome pill burden, nausea and food aversion in pregnancy and are now widely stocked at Walmart, Target, Amazon, pharmacies and grocery chains. Capsules add 244 BPS as premium prenatal systems use them to carry methylfolate, choline, iodine, vitamin D and iron. Tablets are expected to lose 844 BPS, as the format is mature, replenishment-led and exposed to substitution from gummies for swallowing comfort and from capsules for premium nutrient positioning.
seg_share|USA|Product Format|Volume: Gummies are expected to gain 671 BPS of volume share to become the largest format by 2036, as they solve the practical problem of large pills, nausea and food aversion and are now highly visible across mass retail, pharmacy and online channels. Capsules add 218 BPS on the back of premium, practitioner-influenced prenatal systems. Tablets are expected to lose 767 BPS, as growth in this affordable, high-count format is mainly replenishment-led and penetration is already mature.
seg_growth|USA|Product Format|Value: Powder is expected to grow fastest at 13.6% CAGR, followed by liquid at 12.0% and bars at 10.7%, as these prenatal-adjacent formats start from a very small base and benefit from maternal wellness routines, DTC education, pill-free options and convenience occasions such as nausea relief, travel and postpartum nutrition. Gummies, at 9.0%, are the fastest-growing core format, supported by accelerating adoption among younger consumers and preconception users.
seg_opp|USA|Product Format|Value: Gummies are expected to add the largest absolute value over 2026-2036, followed by capsules and tablets. Gummies combine a large base with accelerating adoption among younger consumers, preconception users and shoppers already using gummies in other wellness categories. Capsules continue to add value as methylfolate, higher-choline formulas and subscription routines support premium monthly packs, while tablets remain a large, affordable replenishment format.
seg_attr|USA|Product Format|Value: Tablets followed by gummies are expected to be the most attractive product formats, as tablets retain the largest base across mass retail, drugstores and private-label lines, while gummies pair a similar scale with the highest growth among core formats. Capsules remain a strong premium option, whereas powder, bars and liquid, despite rapid growth, stay small because of taste, mixing, dosing and formulation limits.
seg_share|USA|Product Type|Value: Choline is expected to gain 303 BPS of value share as it becomes the clearest prenatal nutrient upgrade, particularly in premium DTC brands and practitioner-led protocols, while DHA / omega-3 adds 145 BPS on fetal brain and eye development messaging and algae-based options. Probiotics gain 140 BPS from rising microbiome awareness. Multivitamins are expected to lose 252 BPS, as penetration is already high and most growth now comes from add-on products rather than the core formula.
seg_share|USA|Product Type|Volume: Choline is expected to gain 303 BPS of volume share as standalone use rises from a small base and moves from specialist discussion into mainstream prenatal comparison shopping. DHA / omega-3 adds 145 BPS, as many consumers buy a separate DHA softgel when the core prenatal lacks omega-3, and probiotics add 140 BPS. Multivitamins lose 252 BPS because their penetration is already high and growth is steady rather than accelerating.
seg_growth|USA|Product Type|Value: Choline is expected to grow fastest at 12.9% CAGR, as it is still underpenetrated and has become the most visible nutrient upgrade in premium prenatal brands, followed by probiotics at 10.3% on growing demand for digestive comfort and women's health support, and DHA / omega-3 at 7.8% as it extends into gummy and tablet users whose core prenatal lacks omega-3.
seg_opp|USA|Product Type|Value: Multivitamins are expected to add the largest absolute value, followed by DHA / omega-3 and choline. The daily prenatal multivitamin remains the core supplementation routine before conception, during pregnancy and into breastfeeding, and benefits from delayed maternal age, methylfolate upgrades and postpartum continuation. DHA and choline add value as consumers layer them on top of the base prenatal.
seg_attr|USA|Product Type|Value: Multivitamins followed by choline are expected to be the most attractive product types. Multivitamins combine the largest base with predictable, replenishment-driven demand, while choline offers the fastest growth as premium DTC brands and practitioners position it as a key prenatal upgrade. Iron, folate and calcium and mineral products are mature and clinically or diet driven, which limits their attractiveness.
seg_share|USA|Sales Channel|Value: Direct-to-consumer websites are expected to gain 709 BPS of value share and Amazon and online marketplaces 665 BPS, as subscription models convert users before pregnancy confirmation and retain them through monthly shipments, and as online replenishment, Subscribe & Save and easy ingredient comparison capture repeat purchases. Pharmacy and drugstores are expected to lose 750 BPS and mass retail 572 BPS, as these mature channels face pressure from online pricing, DTC subscriptions and shifting discovery behaviour.
seg_share|USA|Sales Channel|Volume: Direct-to-consumer websites are expected to gain 709 BPS of volume share and Amazon and online marketplaces 665 BPS, as personalisation, subscription routines and broader comfort with buying pregnancy supplements digitally move repeat purchases online. Pharmacy and drugstores lose 750 BPS and mass retail 572 BPS, as these store-based channels are mature and growth is driven mainly by replenishment and convenience purchases.
seg_growth|USA|Sales Channel|Value: Direct-to-consumer brand websites are expected to grow fastest at 11.4% CAGR, as subscription models convert consumers before pregnancy confirmation and retain them through postpartum, and as brands use personalisation, methylfolate, choline and clean-label claims to build education-led routines. Amazon and online marketplaces follow at 8.7% on continued online migration and Subscribe & Save behaviour.
seg_opp|USA|Sales Channel|Value: Amazon and online marketplaces are expected to add the largest absolute value, followed by direct-to-consumer websites and mass retail. Prenatal supplements are repeat-purchase products, so online replenishment captures large volumes across capsules, gummies, tablets and DHA softgels, while DTC adds value through subscription retention. Mass retail continues to add value through high-count bottles and private-label availability.
seg_attr|USA|Sales Channel|Value: Amazon and online marketplaces followed by direct-to-consumer websites are expected to be the most attractive sales channels. Amazon combines the largest base with strong growth from online migration, while DTC is the fastest-growing channel on the strength of subscription and personalisation. Pharmacy and mass retail are mature and increasingly pressured by online pricing and subscriptions.
